facts.statement: The species Yangavis confucii was named and described by Wang Min and Zhou Zhonghe in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, the type species Yangavis confucii was named and described by Wang Min and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The specific name confucii honors Confucius and references the family Confuciusornithidae.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Confucius, at the same time referring to the Confuciusornithidae.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the Aptian-aged Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP V18929, was found in a layer of the Yixian Formation dating from the Aptian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an almost complete articulated skeleton that is compressed on a single plate.
facts.quote: It consists of an almost complete articulated skeleton, compressed on a single plate.

facts.statement: Yangavis lived in the area of present China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Yangavis is a basal pygostylian genus, belonging to the Confuciusornithidae, that in the Early Cretaceous lived in the area of present China.

facts.statement: Yangavis is classified as a basal pygostylian genus within the family Confuciusornithidae.
facts.quote: Yangavis is a basal pygostylian genus, belonging to the Confuciusornithidae

facts.statement: Yangavis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Yangavis had a wingspan of approximately half a meter.
facts.quote: Yangavis has a wingspan of about half a metre.

facts.statement: The claw of the second finger in Yangavis was not strongly reduced.
facts.quote: The claw of the second finger is not strongly reduced.

facts.statement: The third toe of Yangavis is longer than its tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: The third toe is longer than the tarsometatarsus.
